text: The number of real solutions of the equation $3\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )-2\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )+5=0$, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$3\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )-2\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )+5=0$

$3\left [\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )^{2}-2\right ]-2\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )+5=0$

Put $x+\frac{1}{x}=t\Rightarrow t\in (-\infty ,-2]\cup [2,\infty )$

$\begin{array}{l} 3t^{2}-2t-1=0 \\  \\ 3t^{2}-3t+t-1=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3t(t-1)+1(t-1)=0\Rightarrow t=1,=-\dfrac{1}{3} \\  \\ \Rightarrow t=1,-\dfrac{1}{3} \\  \\ \because t\in (-\infty ,-2]\cup [2,\infty ) \end{array}$

No real value of $t\Rightarrow$ no real value of $x$.

solution.body:

$\begin{array}{l} =(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2\hat{\mathrm{j}}-4\hat{\mathrm{k}})-λ(4\hat{\mathrm{i}}+3\hat{\mathrm{j}}+5\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\  \\ =(1-4λ)\hat{\mathrm{i}}+(2-3λ)\hat{\mathrm{j}}-(5λ+4)\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\  \\ ⃗{β}_{2}\cdot ⃗{α}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4(1-4λ)+3(2-3λ)-5(5λ+4)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4-16λ+6-9λ-25λ-20=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 50λ=-10 \\  \\ \Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{-1}{5} \\  \\ ⃗{β}_{2}=\left (1+\dfrac{4}{5}\right )\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\left (2+\dfrac{3}{5}\right )\hat{\mathrm{j}}-(-1+4)\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\  \\ ⃗{β}_{2}=\dfrac{9}{5}\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\dfrac{13}{5}\hat{\mathrm{j}}-3\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\  \\ 5⃗{β}_{2}=9\hat{\mathrm{i}}+13\hat{\mathrm{j}}-15\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\  \\ 5⃗{β}_{2}\cdot (\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})=9+13-15=7 \end{array}$

text:
If the system of equations

$x+2y+3z=3$

$4x+3y-4z=4$

$8x+4y-λz=9+μ$

has infinitely many solutions, then the ordered pair ($λ,μ$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For infinite many solution, $\Delta =0$ and $\Delta _{x}=0$

$\begin{array}{lllllll} \Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 4 & -λ \end{array}\right |=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 1(-3λ+16)-2(-4λ+32)+3(16-24)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 16-3λ+8λ-64-24=0\Rightarrow 5λ=72 \\  \\ \therefore λ=\dfrac{72}{5} \\  \\ \Delta _{x}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & -4 \\ 9+μ & 4 & -λ \end{array}\right |=0 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 3(-3λ+16)-2(-4λ+36+4μ)+3(16-27-3μ)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow -9λ+48+8λ-72-8μ-33-9μ=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow -λ-17μ=57 \\  \\ \Rightarrow -17μ=57+λ \\  \\ \therefore -μ=\dfrac{57+\frac{72}{5}}{17} \\  \\ \Rightarrow μ=\dfrac{-357}{85}=\dfrac{-21}{5} \end{array}$

$\text{Thus,}(λ,μ)\equiv \left (\frac{72}{5},\frac{-21}{5}\right )$

text: The set of all values of $a$ for which $\lim _{x\to a}([x-5]-[2x+2])=0$, where [$α$] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $α$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to a}([x-5]-[2x+2])=0$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to a}([x]-5-[2x]-2)=0$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to a}[x]-[2x]-7=0$

Case 1 :

If $a\in \left [n,n+\frac{1}{2}\right )$

then $\lim _{x\to a}([x]-[2x]-7)=0$

$\Rightarrow n-2n-7=0$

$\Rightarrow n=-7$

$\therefore$ $a\in [-7,-6.5)$

Case 2 :

If $a\in \left [n+\frac{1}{2},n+1\right )$

then $\lim _{x\to a}([x]-[2x]-7)=0$

$\Rightarrow n-(2n+1)-7=0$

$\Rightarrow -n-8=0$

$\Rightarrow n=-8$

$\therefore$ $a\in [-7.5,-7)$

$R.H.L=\lim _{x\to -7.5^{+}}([x]-[2x]-7)$

$=-8-(-15)-7$

$=-8+15-7=0$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & L.H.L=\lim _{x\to -7.5^{-}}([x]-[2x]-7) \\  \\  & =-8-(-16)-7 \\  \\  & =-8+16-7=1 \end{array}$

$\therefore$ R.H.L $\neq$ L.H.L

$\therefore$ At x = -7.5, limit does not exist.

$\therefore$ $a\in (-7.5,-6.5)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(x^{2}-3y^{2})dx+3xydy=0,y(1)=1$. Then $6y^{2}(e)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\left (x^{2}-3y^{2}\right )dx+3xydy=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}dx-3y^{2}dx+3xydy=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x^{2}dx}{3xdx}-\frac{3y^{2}dx}{3xdx}+\frac{3xydy}{3xdx}=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{3}-\frac{y^{2}}{x}+y\frac{dy}{dx}=0$

Let $y^{2}=t$

$2y\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dt}{dx}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\frac{dt}{dx}-\frac{t}{x}+\frac{x}{3}=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dt}{dx}-\frac{2t}{x}=-\frac{2x}{3}$

This is linear Differential Equation.

$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int -\frac{2}{x}dx}=e^{-2\ln |x|}=e^{\ln \frac{1}{x2}}=\frac{1}{x^{2}}$

So, $t\cdot \frac{1}{x^{2}}=\int \frac{1}{x^{2}}\left (\frac{-2x}{3}\right )dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}=\frac{-2}{3}\ln |x|+C$ 

When, $x=1,y=1$

$1=\frac{-2}{3}\ln (1)+C\Rightarrow C=1$

$\therefore \frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}=\frac{-2}{3}\ln |x|+1$

At $x=e,\frac{y^{2}(e)}{e^{2}}=\frac{-2}{3}+1$

$\Rightarrow y^{2}(e)=\frac{e^{2}}{3}$

$\Rightarrow 6y^{2}(e)=2e^{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

Now sum of terms equidistant from beginning and end is 1

text: The value of $\left (\frac{1+\sin \frac{2π}{9}+i\cos \frac{2π}{9}}{1+\sin \frac{2π}{9}-i\cos \frac{2π}{9}}\right )^{3}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\sin \dfrac{2π}{9}=\cos \dfrac{5π}{18}$ and $\cos \dfrac{2π}{9}=\sin \dfrac{5π}{18}$, write $θ=\dfrac{5π}{18}$. The numerator is

$1+\cos θ+i\sin θ=2\cos ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}+2i\sin \dfrac{θ}{2}\cos \dfrac{θ}{2}=2\cos \dfrac{θ}{2}e^{iθ/2}$

The denominator $1+\cos θ-i\sin θ$ is its conjugate, $2\cos \dfrac{θ}{2}e^{-iθ/2}$, and $\cos \dfrac{θ}{2}\neq 0$, so the fraction equals

$\dfrac{e^{iθ/2}}{e^{-iθ/2}}=e^{iθ}=e^{i5π/18}$

Cubing,

$\left (e^{i5π/18}\right )^{3}=e^{i5π/6}=\cos \dfrac{5π}{6}+i\sin \dfrac{5π}{6}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{i}{2}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\sqrt{3}-i\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: $\int\limits _{\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}\frac{48}{\sqrt{9-4x^{2}}}dx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}\frac{48}{\sqrt{9-4x^{2}}}dx$

We have $\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}=\sin ^{-1}\frac{x}{a}+C$

Hence $\int\limits _{\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}\frac{48}{\sqrt{9-4x^{2}}}dx=\frac{48}{2}\times \left [\sin ^{-1}\frac{2x}{3}\right ]_{\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}}^{\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}}$

$=24\times \left [\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}\right )-\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{2}{3}\times \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\right )\right ]$
$=24\times \left [\sin ^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\sin ^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$=24\times \left (\frac{π}{3}-\frac{π}{4}\right )$

$=24\times \frac{π}{12}=2π$

text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x+\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{y-\sqrt{6}}{3}=\frac{z-\sqrt{6}}{4}$ and $\frac{x-λ}{3}=\frac{y-2\sqrt{6}}{4}=\frac{z+2\sqrt{6}}{5}$ is 6, then the square of sum of all possible values of $λ$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Shortest distance between the lines

 $\frac{x+\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{y-\sqrt{6}}{3}=\frac{z-\sqrt{6}}{4}$

 $\frac{x-λ}{3}=\frac{y-2\sqrt{6}}{4}=\frac{z+2\sqrt{6}}{5}$ is 6

Vector along line of shortest distance

 $=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \mathrm{i} & \mathrm{j} & \mathrm{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \end{array}\right |,\Rightarrow -\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\mathrm{k}$ (its magnitude is $\sqrt{6}$ )

Now $\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\left |\begin{array}{lll} \sqrt{6}+λ & \sqrt{6} & -3\sqrt{6} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \end{array}\right |=\pm 6$ 

$\Rightarrow λ=-2\sqrt{6},10\sqrt{6}$

So, square of sum of these values

$=(10\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{6})^{2}=(8\sqrt{6})^{2}=384$

text: Let $f$ be a differentiable function defined on $\left [0,\frac{π}{2}\right ]$ such that $f(x)>0$ and $f(x)+\int\limits _{0}^{x}f(t)\sqrt{1-(\log _{e}f(t))^{2}}dt=e,\forall x\in \left [0,\frac{π}{2}\right ]$. Then $\left (6\log _{e}f\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )\right )^{2}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)+\int\limits _{0}^{x}f(t)\sqrt{1-(\log _{e}f(t))^{2}}dt=e...(1)$

So, $f(0)=e$

Now differentiate w.r. to $x$

$\begin{array}{l} f^{'}(x)+f(x)\sqrt{1-(\log _{e}f(x))^{2}}=0 \\  \\ \dfrac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)\sqrt{1-(\log _{e}f(x))^{2}}}=-1 \end{array}$

Let $\log _{e}f(x)=t$

$\therefore \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}=-x+c$

$\Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}t=-x+c$

Now $f(0)=e\Rightarrow t=1$ So, $c=\frac{π}{2}$

$\therefore t=\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}-x\right )=\cos x\left (\because x\in \left [0,\frac{π}{2}\right ]\right )$

$\therefore \left (6\log _{e}f\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )\right )^{2}=27$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

Area $=\int\limits _{0}^{3}\left (2y-y^{2}\right )-(-y)dy$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{3}\left (3y-y^{2}\right )dy$

$\left. \begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{3y^{2}}{2}-\dfrac{y^{3}}{3}\right ]_{0}^{3} \\  \\ =\dfrac{27}{2}-9 \\  \\ =\dfrac{27-18}{2}=\dfrac{9}{2}=A \end{array}$

$8A=\frac{9}{2}\times 8=36$ sq. units

text: Three urns A, B and C contain 4 red, 6 black; 5 red, 5 black; and $λ$ red, 4 black balls respectively. One of the urns is selected at random and a ball is drawn. If the ball drawn is red and the probability that it is drawn from urn C is 0.4 then the square of the length of the side of the largest equilateral triangle, inscribed in the parabola $y^{2}=λx$ with one vertex at the vertex of the parabola, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$E_{1}$ : Ball is drawn from urn $A(4R+6B)$

$E_{2}:$ Ball is drawn from urn $B(5R+5B)$

$E_{3}$ : Ball is drawn from urn $C(λR+4B)$

$A\to$ Ball drawn is red.

Required probability $=P\left (\frac{E_{3}}{A}\right )$

$=\frac{\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{λ}{λ+4}}{\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{4}{10}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{5}{10}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{λ}{λ+4}}=\frac{2}{5}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{10λ}{19λ+36}=\frac{2}{5}$

$\Rightarrow λ=6$

So, parabola $y^{2}=6x$

Let side length of the triangle be $l$.


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \tan 30^{\circ }=\dfrac{3t}{\frac{3}{2}t^{2}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\dfrac{2}{t} \\  \\ \therefore t=2\sqrt{3} \\  \\ \text{So,}\left (\dfrac{3}{2}t^{2},3t\right ) \\  \\ =(18,6\sqrt{3}) \end{array}$

$\text{Now,}l^{2}=18^{2}+(6\sqrt{3})^{2}=324+108=432$
